newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firmer but trade still light.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firmer but trade still light.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed after an overnight recovery on Thursday but trade continued to be light, dealers said.

"We marked up at the open, benefitting from a slightly better tone in the U.S. market," a dealer said. "But volumes are light and there's not much in the way of dramatic news around to motivate investors."
Irish bonds were tracking Germany quite closely and continuing to trade well in a European context, dealers said.
Subdued UK inflation data released earlier had had no impact on the Irish market.
In the U.S., Treasury bond futures gained nearly a half-point in early New York trade as a rise in jobless claims suggested employment growth slowing.

"At the moment I think what we're seeing is a tentative recovery," one dealer said. "Bond markets have experienced a bit of a shakeout recently and they're just beginning to stabilise. In Ireland we're still basking in the afterglow of Tuesday's successful auction."
On Tuesday, an auction by the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) of 150 million Irish pounds of the eight percent bond due 2006 was covered 5.15 times.

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 14 pence from Wednesday's close at 102.24 to yield 5.91 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 25 pence from the close at 109.00 to yield 6.66 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 139 basis points over Germany in the five-year area and 85 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area.

Looking ahead, the March wholesale price index, due for release by the Central Statistics Office at 1200 local time tomorrow, would be of interest, dealers said. -- Kevin Smith, Dublin newsroom + 353 1 661 3377
